construct: 31 adjacent same-shape siblings (a wrapping flex run), the LAST carrying a distinct paint (rgb(32, 160, 96))
why: A MONTH. This is the case the owner named: with no forward repetition rule, a month is ~200 flat nodes rather than a cell component with 31 instances. The flat emission is not, by itself, a wrong picture - so this case does NOT measure node count, it measures whether the 31st cell (the odd one, e.g. 'today') survives the walk at all. A month that draws 31 identical cells and loses the one that differs is the recognisability failure, and it is invisible to any instrument that counts nodes.

mustHave: the 31st box is a visibly different colour (green) from the other 30 (pale blue-grey)
the boxes wrap into multiple rows rather than one long line
all 31 boxes are the same size (16x16)

predictedWall.status: PROPOSED - no existing code covers this
predictedWall.why: There is NO forward repetition rule. The inverse exists (core/propose-figma.ts, >=3 adjacent same-component instances -> part.repeat) but nothing in the capture direction turns N repeated siblings into a component plus instances, so a month is emitted flat. The flat emission is not itself the failure I predict; what I predict is that at 31 siblings the union naming in extract/computed/anatomy.ts nameUnion() - which suffixes duplicates a, a-2 ... a-31 - plus the per-part folding downstream will treat the 31 near-identical siblings as one repeated shape and fold the ODD sibling's distinct fill away with them. I searched spec/channel-table.json, spec/door-register.json, spec/lowering.json and spec/grammar-coverage.json for a repetition code and there is none; FC-CELL-FRAMING / FC-CELL-INK-LOST are composition-corpus slot fills, not this.
